clue.text: Chartreuse, drunk by wrong set, is object of a pirate's dig?

indicators.note: a drunk person is all over the place, so the letters of the liqueur's name are jumbled
set wrongly means its three letters are put in the wrong order

explanation.surface: A liqueur-loving crew knocks back Chartreuse while a pirate digs for his prize.
explanation.walkthrough: The ten letters of CHARTREUSE rearranged give TREASURECH, and SET rearranged gives EST.
explanation.definitionFit: Pirates in stories bury a box of gold and jewels and later dig it up, so it is the thing their spades hunt for.

clue.text: It provides proof of ace group of detectives attending sports event

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for ace on playing cards
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of a British police force
a Test is an international cricket or rugby match

explanation.surface: Police detectives turn up at a sports fixture to gather evidence.
explanation.walkthrough: A Test match is the top-level international game in cricket, played between national sides.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names a decisive trial that settles whether something is genuine, as acid once tested gold.

clue.text: Female player's cause

parts.note: a player on stage is a performer in a play

explanation.surface: An actress takes up a cause.
explanation.definitionFit: A contributing element that brings something about is a synonym for one cause of it.

clue.text: Soldier's round embedded in battleaxe

indicators.note: something embedded in another thing sits inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a battleaxe or dragon is a fierce, domineering woman
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A soldier's bullet lodges in a battleaxe weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'battleaxe' looks like a weapon but is the slang for a formidable woman, a dragon.
explanation.definitionFit: Historically a mounted infantryman, the word names a kind of soldier.

clue.text: Director of 20, covering society (South-east)

indicators.note: one piece covering another wraps around it

parts.note: a score is twenty
SE is the compass abbreviation for south-east

explanation.surface: A film director of entry 20 is linked to a society in the south-east of England.
explanation.walkthrough: '20' looks like a cross-reference to another entry but is simply the number, a score.
explanation.definitionFit: Martin Scorsese is an American film-maker, famous for Taxi Driver and GoodFellas.

clue.text: Hidden optical faculty all used up?

definitions.meaning: concealed where nobody can see it
having run out of one's eyesight, read whimsically

explanation.surface: A hidden vision that has been completely exhausted.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means beyond view; read literally it says one has no vision left, like being out of milk.

clue.text: Opposition chiefly to bench aid was misplaced

indicators.note: letters that were misplaced have been put in the wrong positions, so the four words are jumbled

explanation.surface: The Opposition leaders head to the bench, but the aid went astray.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misplaced' rearranges all the letters of TO BENCH AID WAS; 'chiefly' belongs to the definition, since the body is the opposition's leading members.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain the senior opposition spokespeople who mirror government ministers form this body.

clue.text: Padding taken advantage of by such relaxed solvers?

definitions.text: Padding taken advantage of by such relaxed solvers?

parts.words: Padding taken advantage of by such relaxed solvers?
parts.note: fans of crime fiction who solve cases from a comfy upholstered seat, the padding being the cushions they sink into

explanation.surface: Puzzle solvers relax on comfortable padding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'solvers' suggests crossword solvers, but here they solve mysteries.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes amateurs who work out crimes from home, reading or watching rather than investigating.

clue.text: Who idly views analysis aid number two — "full of cheap rubbish"

parts.note: the psychoanalyst's patient lies on a couch

indicators.note: one piece full of another contains it

parts.note: a number two is a child's euphemism for a poo
tat is cheap, tasteless goods

explanation.surface: A therapy aid, number two in a list, is stuffed with cheap junk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'analysis' means psychoanalysis; 'number two' is the nursery word for faeces.
explanation.definitionFit: A lazy person who spends hours idly watching television fits the phrase 'who idly views'.

clue.text: Leave genetic material to regress after sulphur hazard

indicators.note: the reversed pieces come after the sulphur symbol

parts.note: S is the chemical symbol for sulphur

indicators.note: to regress is to go backwards, so these letters are read from the end

parts.note: to part is to leave
DNA is the genetic material of cells

explanation.surface: Instructions to let genetic material degrade after a sulphur leak, a chemical hazard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to regress' turns the pair round together, giving ANDTRAP; 'hazard' is the golfing sense, not a chemical danger.
explanation.definitionFit: A golf bunker is one of the hazards on a course, in the American name for it.

clue.text: Court crime officer is after "Cat", once a champion driver

indicators.note: the courting and officer pieces come after the cat

parts.note: a tiger is a big cat
to woo is to court
DS is a detective sergeant

explanation.surface: A police officer chases a cat burglar who was once a champion racing driver.
explanation.walkthrough: 'driver' is a golf club, not a motorist.
explanation.definitionFit: The American golfer was world number one for years; a driver is a golf club and also a golfer driving off.

clue.text: Top content of rookery?

definitions.meaning: to top someone is slang for killing them
a group of crows is called by this collective noun, and rooks are crows

explanation.definitionFit: The word means to kill, and is also the collective noun for a flock of crows, the birds of a rookery.

clue.text: See 8
Stitched up, confess to taking in lines

indicators.note: one piece taking in another holds it inside

parts.note: to own up is to confess
verse is lines of poetry

explanation.surface: Someone framed confesses to taking in some lines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stitched up' suggests being framed, but it is the sewing sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Sewn over an edge with stitches means sewn up, a needlework sense of the phrase.

clue.text: Declare it's correct to switch first and third

indicators.note: the first and third letters of the synonym change places, which turns the opening trio around

parts.note: to rectify is to correct

explanation.surface: Claim it is right to swap the first and third items.
explanation.walkthrough: In RECTIFY, the R and C swap, giving CER at the start.
explanation.definitionFit: To formally confirm something as true is to declare it officially, a synonym.

clue.text: Domino cut by half-opened scissors, ones on the extreme right?

indicators.note: one piece cut by another is split open to take it in

parts.note: Fats Domino was an American rock and roll pianist

indicators.note: only the opening half of the word is used

explanation.surface: A domino tile is sliced by a pair of scissors only half open.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Domino' looks like a game tile but is the singer.
explanation.definitionFit: Supporters of authoritarian nationalism sit at the far end of the political spectrum, hence the playful question.

clue.text: Deposit unwelcome from this main fool

parts.note: the main is the sea
to gull someone is to fool them

explanation.surface: A fool at sea is the source of an unwelcome deposit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deposit' is a bird dropping landing on someone.
explanation.definitionFit: A coastal bird notorious for leaving droppings on people below is described by the definition.

clue.text: At the end of the day, it's viewed as wealth so wasted

definitions.text: At the end of the day, it's viewed

indicators.note: wealth that is wasted is squandered, so these letters are scattered

explanation.surface: At the end of the day, wealth is seen as squandered.
explanation.definitionFit: A late-night television programme is watched at the close of the day.

clue.text: See 7
Re-engineering basics when returning x-coordinate

indicators.note: re-engineering something rebuilds it in a new arrangement
returning means coming back, so this word is read backwards

parts.note: as means when

explanation.surface: Re-engineering the basics when coming back to a coordinate.
explanation.walkthrough: BASICS rearranged gives ABSCIS; AS read backwards gives SA.
explanation.definitionFit: In a graph the horizontal distance from the vertical axis is the mathematical term for this coordinate.

clue.text: Rag Maureen immersed in stream

indicators.note: something immersed in water sits inside it

parts.note: a beck is a stream in northern England
Mo is short for Maureen

explanation.surface: A rag belonging to Maureen gets dunked in a stream.
explanation.walkthrough: BECK is the northern English dialect word for a stream.
explanation.definitionFit: To rag is to tease or ridicule, as is to mock someone.

clue.text: See 9
Incomplete design made by baby's feet?

indicators.note: an incomplete word lacks its last letter

parts.note: a pattern is a design

explanation.surface: A baby's feet make an unfinished pattern.
explanation.definitionFit: The rapid light tapping sound of tiny feet is what the familiar phrase about tiny feet describes.

clue.text: Philosopher's permit is useless outside Channel Isles

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go outside the islands' abbreviation
useless means no good, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: CI is the abbreviation for the Channel Islands

explanation.surface: A philosopher's permit is no use outside the Channel Islands.
explanation.definitionFit: A thinker who holds that knowledge comes from experience is a type of philosopher.

clue.text: See 2
See 10
See 1
Lift to reveal cracks

indicators.note: cracks breaks into pieces, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A lift is opened up to show its cracks.
explanation.definitionFit: The American word for the cabin that carries people between floors is a synonym.
